examples.text: Я хотел постучаться и не рассчитал.
examples.trans: I wanted to knock and misjudged my strength.

examples.text: Мы всё точно рассчитали.
examples.trans: We calculated everything accurately.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.text: В комнату вдруг входит грозная Марина.
examples.trans: Formidable Marina suddenly enters the room.

examples.text: Знаешь, я тут серьёзно думаю.
examples.trans: You know, I am thinking seriously here.

examples.text: Значит, штаны просто-напросто сами могли упасть!
examples.trans: That means the pants could have simply fallen down by themselves!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И она сразу сказала мне да!
examples.trans: And she immediately said yes to me!

examples.text: Сеня и Федя, готовьте закуски!
examples.trans: Senya and Fedya, prepare the snacks!

examples.text: Зачем так сильно расстраиваться сейчас?
examples.trans: Why get so upset right now?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это он всю жизнь хитро подставлял Макса!
examples.trans: He is the one who slyly framed Max his whole life!

examples.text: Максим, знаешь, что я понял за жизнь?
examples.trans: Maxim, do you know what I have realized over my life?

examples.text: Такая жизнь.
examples.trans: That's life.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А вот если бы ты меня убил?
examples.trans: And what if you had killed me?

examples.text: Если бы меня вдруг не стало?
examples.trans: If I were suddenly gone?

examples.text: Папа, а если бы она тебе отказала?
examples.trans: Dad, and what if she had turned you down?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Женщина, не буди во мне зверя!
examples.trans: Woman, do not wake the beast in me!

examples.text: Эта женщина навсегда разбила моё сердце.
examples.trans: That woman broke my heart forever.

examples.text: Если женщина ненавидит, значит, ей всё равно?
examples.trans: If a woman hates you, does it mean she does not care?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'навидеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hates', paired with 'возненавидеть'.

examples.text: За что ты меня ненавидишь?
examples.trans: Why do you hate me?

examples.text: Я ненавижу понедельник.
examples.trans: I hate Mondays.

examples.text: Скажи мне в глаза. За что ты меня так ненавидишь?
examples.trans: Say it to my face. Why do you hate me so much?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Значит, штаны просто-напросто сами могли упасть!
examples.trans: That means the pants could have simply fallen down by themselves!

examples.text: Значит, тем вечером всё было именно так.
examples.trans: So, that evening everything happened just like this.

examples.text: Значит, на самом деле было вот так.
examples.trans: So, in reality it happened like this.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И она сразу сказала мне да!
examples.trans: And she immediately said yes to me!

examples.text: Зачем ты кидаешь в меня макаронами?
examples.trans: Why are you throwing macaroni at me?

examples.text: Папа, а если бы она тебе отказала?
examples.trans: Dad, and what if she had turned you down?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ты правда хотел меня сейчас ударить?
examples.trans: Did you really want to hit me just now?

examples.text: Я же всегда говорю только правду.
examples.trans: I always tell only the truth.

examples.text: Кто этим водителям права даёт?
examples.trans: Who gives driver's licenses to these drivers?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пойдём со мной в кабинет, Максим.
examples.trans: Come with me to the office, Maxim.

examples.text: Нет, дорогая, конечно же нет.
examples.trans: No, darling, of course not.

examples.text: У меня дома просто нет шансов.
examples.trans: I simply have no chance at home.
